nodes.title: Normalized Siegel analytic coefficients
nodes.statement: Fix g≥1 and rational r>0. Write I=Iw_GLg for the upper Iwahori over Z_p, I+=its diagonal-mod-p subgroup, M_s={1+E:‖E‖≤p^(−s)} over C_p, s=r+1, and G_s=I M_s. For a diagonal character κ with a unit-valued analytic extension to T^(s), define Cκ,r as the A-Banach module of analytic functions on G_s satisfying f(ℓb)=κ(b)f(ℓ) for b∈B∩G_s, κ trivial on the upper unipotent. Its norm is the finite-chart Gauss norm on the opposite-unipotent variables u_ij/p, with chart radius p^(−r); Cκ,r+ is that norm unit ball. For h∈H_s=I+ M_s define ρ_D(h)f(ℓ)=f(hᵀℓ). This is an isometric left action preserving the Gauss lattice. Products map Cκ,r×Cλ,r→Cκλ,r; affinoid scalar change and radius restriction use the analytic function modules on these same normalized charts.
hypotheses: A is a reduced uniform affinoid over C_p, A+ is its power-bounded unit ball; use the supplied completed coefficient sheaf on a geometric base.
The character and its inverse are power-bounded on the chosen torus extension. For the O8 family retain w>1+r_U and put r=w; this suffices for the required character extension.
The group neighbourhood is entrywise p^(−(r+1)); the normalized lower coordinates are r-analytic. No action of I+ M_r on the whole module is asserted.
proofSteps: Use Iwahori factorization on I M_(r+1); after division of each lower entry by p its opposite cell is the p^(−r)-thickening of Z_p^d. Apply LAD fixed-radius multivariable analytic functions with the affinoid Gauss lattice.

Cut out right Borel equivariance. Left translation by hᵀ preserves the domain, since transpose preserves H_(r+1) and this group lies in G_(r+1). Its chart maps and inverse have integral analytic coefficients, as does the unit-valued character multiplier; hence translation preserves the Gauss unit ball in both directions.

Transpose reverses products, giving ρ_D(h1h2)=ρ_D(h1)ρ_D(h2). Multiply equivariant functions to obtain the product-weight pairing. Use LAD completed tensor and chart restriction for coefficient and radius maps.
acceptance: In genus 1 the space is the rank-one κ-character module, with its actual Gauss lattice.
In genus 2, lower coordinate t=u21/p has analytic radius p^(−r), so the unnormalized entry radius is p^(−(r+1)).

Pointwise multiplication on the full Iwahori sends weight κ to weight κ² and does not close a nontrivial fixed weight. Restriction to the opposite unipotent separately transports a Banach algebra structure to that space.

sources.match: The source normalizes each lower coordinate by p. The entry radius and action group here include the resulting shift; finding E-O8-17 records the stronger printed action that fails.
Analytic induction lives on a genuine group thickening and is modeled by its opposite-cell analytic functions.

nodes.title: BP and Siegel induction conventions
nodes.statement: For M=GL_g and M1=Iw_GLg, let BP use the character λ_BP=w0,M(κ_D⁻¹). On the same domain G_n=M1 M_n, its right-Borel rule (w0,M λ_BP)(b⁻¹) equals κ_D(b). The identity on functions is an isometry between BP V_(λ_BP)^(n-an) and C_(κ_D),r for r=n−1>0. With τ(h)=h^(−T), the actions satisfy ρ_D(h)=ρ_BP(τ(h)), h∈I+ M_n. Algebraic restriction transports through this identity and τ, after the B2 highest-weight conversion; the central character is retained. Integer n is cofinal in the rational radius system.
hypotheses: Use one split GL_g, the same upper Borel, Weyl element and unnormalized matrix-entry domain in both models.
The BP module uses inverse left translation; the Siegel model uses transpose left translation. Restrict to the strict subgroup, which is stable under transpose inverse.

This adapter concerns M1 open Iwahori. The general closed, possibly non-open M1 in O0/analytic-induced-coefficients is unchanged. Positive-torus normalizations and distribution duals retain their original BP conventions.
proofSteps: Compute w0,M²=1 on torus characters and evaluate at b⁻¹, giving the identical Borel equivariance relation.
Identify BP’s lower entry variable with p times the Siegel normalized variable. The two affinoid domains and Gauss norms then agree for r=n−1.

Since τ is a group automorphism of the strict subgroup and τ(h)⁻¹=hᵀ, inverse left translation becomes the desired transpose action. Restriction of regular algebraic functions is equivariant under this conversion and injective because an open p-adic cell is Zariski dense.
acceptance: For g=1 λ_BP=κ_D⁻¹; the character action on each side is κ_D(h).
For g=2 and κ_D=diag-character (k1,k2), λ_BP has exponents (−k2,−k1), not (k1,k2).
Under a scalar h=aI the transported algebraic action keeps its central exponent; it is not silently dualized.

sources.match: Right Borel equivariance, inverse left translation, finite twists and the algebraic restriction map.
The normalized analytic chart and transpose action are converted explicitly into the BP convention.

nodes.title: Siegel factor neighbourhood bound
nodes.statement: For γ=[A,B;C,D] in the group-theoretic strict GSp_2g Iwahori, and Z=Z0+E with Z0∈Mat_g(Z_p), ‖E‖≤p^(−w), w>0, put J=A+ZC and J0=A+Z0C. Then J0∈Iw_GLg+ and ‖J−J0‖≤p^(−(w+1)), because C∈p Mat_g(Z_p). Consequently J∈Iw_GLg+ M_(w+1), its determinant is a unit, and the same neighbourhood is stable under transpose inverse. Thus the occurring geometric factors act on the full normalized w-analytic coefficient module Cκ,w of O0 without enlarging its analytic radius.
hypotheses: g≥1; use the entrywise maximum norm on C_p matrices and its scalar extension on each supplied affinoid chart.
Strict Iwahori means diagonal reduction modulo p in the full GSp group, so A mod p is invertible diagonal and C mod p=0.
Z0 need not be a Lagrangian matrix; its sole purpose is an integral approximation to Z. Apply the result locally on each period-chart ball.
proofSteps: Reduce J0 modulo p: the C term vanishes, giving the invertible diagonal reduction of A. J0 and its inverse therefore have integral entries.
The ultrametric product estimate gives ‖EC‖≤p^(−w)p⁻¹. Factor J=J0(1+J0⁻¹EC). This is a factorization in Iw+ M_(w+1).

Inversion and transpose preserve the diagonal-mod-p subgroup and the deep principal neighbourhood; the analytic coefficient action of O0/siegel-analytic-coefficients is therefore defined on all these factors.
acceptance: In genus 1, γ=[1,0;p,1] gives J=1+pZ, exhibiting the extra factor p exactly.
If C=0 then J=A and there is no analytic error term.
For the full upper Iwahori A mod p can be upper triangular with a nonzero strict-upper entry; the conclusion that J0 is diagonal modulo p specifically uses strict Iwahori.

sources.locator: §2.1 pp7–9; §2.3 p15; Definition 2.5.3 p19; Remark 3.1.15 p25

nodes.title: Effective arithmetic coefficient descent
nodes.statement: On the hybrid Hilbert tower, use the completed group E(p^n)=(Γ0(p^n)×Δ(p∞N))/Z∞, with Z∞ the closure of U_N and z↦(zI,z²). On the arithmetic tower use PΓ0(p^n)=Γ0(p^n)/Z∞. For κ=w²(t∘N)⁻¹, the continuous multipliers κ(cz+d)⁻¹w(x̄) and κ(cz+d)⁻¹w(det γ) descend to these groups and agree with the independently defined O4 presentation equalizers. Requiring equivariance on the dense positive-unit subgroup of E(p^n) is equivalent to requiring it on the entire completed deck group.
hypotheses: F totally real, N≥4 prime to p, and the actual finite-level quotients/tower actions supplied by H4/S5.
The character family and automorphy factor are admitted as in O2; the coefficient topology is separated and the action continuous.
Only the hybrid tower has an O_p×-valued eβ. On the arithmetic tower the pairing is defined modulo the positive-unit closure.
proofSteps: Apply O4/arithmetic-representatives to all U_N, then pass to its closure. The central multiplier is t(Nz)=1.
Use S5’s inverse limit of finite effective deck groups, rather than replacing it by its dense abstract subgroup.

For each section, the equality of its two continuous translates is closed in the deck group, since the section module is Hausdorff. Equality on a dense subgroup is equivalent to equality everywhere, locally and compatibly with restriction.
acceptance: For F=Q the fine-level congruence-unit group is trivial and the arithmetic kernel has no extra spurious p-adic units.
Check both positive and mixed-sign norm-one congruence units; total positivity is not part of the kernel definition.
At N=2 the norm-one proof fails for −1∈Z×, showing the explicit fine-level condition is necessary for this argument.

sources.match: Use the section multipliers with the corrected effective quotient supplied by H4/S5. Norm congruence extends the positive-unit cancellation to all congruence units.
